thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Auto-detect: sudden p99 spike for streaming (/v1/stream) in eu-west-2. p95 also up. Multiple downstream clients reporting stalled frames. Alert ID: 6965432101. Dash: https://dash.redwood/alerts/6965432101

sara: I'm on call. Joining bridge. Any recent infra pushes to eu-west-2?

deploy-bot: Recent deployments affecting eu-west-2:
- router-policy-adjust-2026-03-15 applied 7m ago (75% roll)
- balancer-weights-hotfix applied 3h ago (100%)

tony: grabbing perf slices. Early signs: increased "router.reassigns" and a small cluster of shards showing >85% CPU. Also seeing streaming reconnects spike. Logs:```
[router] region=eu-west-2 shard=shard-07 reassign=48 last5m
[client] connection_reset streaming=client-4235 count=312
```

nina: that reassigns number is alarming. If policy-adjust altered fallback order, we could be bouncing a set of keys across hot hosts. That causes head-of-line blocking for streaming sessions.

sre-oncall: can we triage with a short mitigation: divert new streaming sessions in eu-west-2 to eu-west-1 (warm standby)? Prefer rolling-routing override over global rollback so other traffic unaffected.

sara: agree. Tony, apply routing override, and set TTL=10m. Also start graceful drain on the top 3 hot hosts. Keep a watch on p99.

tony: running now:
```
redwoodctl routing set-override --region eu-west-2 --path /v1/stream --destination eu-west-1-streaming-pool --ttl 10m --by sara
redwoodctl host drain --region eu-west-2 --host host-07 --reason "hot-evac"
redwoodctl host drain --region eu-west-2 --host host-11 --reason "hot-evac"
redwoodctl host drain --region eu-west-2 --host host-02 --reason "hot-evac"
```

ops-bot: Override applied and hosts marked draining.

tony: p99 dropped from ~2.9s -> 1.1s within ~70s after override, reconnects down 82%. Egress queue length reduced.

support-agent: Customer impact: 5 customers with active streaming SLAs filed errors. Top two affected (ORG 334, ORG 119) experienced ~6 minutes of degraded frames. Opening support tickets and drafting notice.

nina: quick analysis: router-policy-adjust included a weight normalization change and changed the tie-breaker when two shards have similar load. In practice this created a flip-flop for a subset of hot keys because our hotkey detector thresholds are slightly misaligned with the new tie-breaker window. Result: repeated reassignment loop for ~2% of keys hitting the streaming endpoints -> tail stalls.

eng-router: confirm: tie-breaker uses last-seen-seed if diff < 2%. Policy-adjust inadvertently used a floating point compare that underflows in some envs. Fix in PR#5247 (adding epsilon) ready.

sre-oncall: action list short-term:
- keep override until global rollback or patch deployed
- extend draining until hosts <5% active streaming sessions
- throttle clients that exhibit aggressive reconnects (rate-limit reconnects)
- contact deployments team to halt router-policy-adjust rollout

sara: @deploy-bot pause rollout for router-policy-adjust in all regions.

deploy-bot: Rollout pause issued for router-policy-adjust. Current rollout: 75% -> paused. No partial rollback yet.

eng-router: we'll push PR#5247 hotfix to canary in staging, then to 5% in prod. ETA 30m for canary, 60m for cautious ramp if green.

tony: additional mitigations: added per-key eviction for KV cache for the hot keys to break the reassignment cycle. This is low-impact and reversible. Implemented via emergency flag:```
redwoodctl kvcache evict --region eu-west-2 --predicate "key in hotlist_696543" --confirm
```

support-agent: sending customer notices now: short note + ETA for full resolution (we estimate 1h to complete canary + verification).

sara: handing monitoring to tony and nina for 90m. I'll stay on-call for escalations. Create incident ticket and assign owners.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-696543. Owner=tony, watcher=nina, watch_until=6965438100. Bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/6965432101

tony: status update 18m: canary in staging passed perf checks. p99 in eu-west-2 stable at ~1.0s for last 12m. No new reconnect flurry. We'll validate hotkey eviction logs and then roll patch to 5% in prod.

eng-router: rolling patch to 5% now. Will monitor key reassign rate and misroute ratio.

tony: patch at 5% shows improved tie-breaker stability; reassigns dropped 93% on patched hosts. Rolling to 100% paused for 15m observation window.

sre-oncall: if 15m stays green, proceed to full rollout. Keep guardrails: automated rollback if misroute >1% or p99 >1.5s sustained for 3m.

support-agent: updated impacted customer tickets with mitigation summary and next steps.

nina: post-incident follow-ups (for postmortem):
- add epsilon test to tie-breaker logic + unit tests for low-diff scenarios
- make canary policy for router policy changes mandatory (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with automated heatmap checks between steps
- add hotkey oscillation detection alarm (reassigns > 10/min for keyset size < 1000)
- review our streaming session reconnect throttling default (lower aggressive retries)

sara: closing active bridge in 10m if no regression. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Alert cleared. Incident remains in monitoring state until owners close INC-696543 with postmortem.
